text: of those taking high doses) • intermediate risk (4% or less): • felbamate • levetiracetam • tiagabine • lower risk (less than 1%; some might actually have pos- itive effects on mood): • carbamazepine • ethosuximide • gabapentin • lamotrigine • oxcarbazepine • phenytoin • pregabalin • valproate In January 2008, the FDA issued an alert16 after analysis of 199 placebo-controlled studies of antiepileptic drugs in the management of not only epilepsy but also psychiatric dis- orders (including bipolar disorder and depression) and oth- er conditions such as migraine and neuropathic pain. This analysis, which involved 27 863 drug-treated patients and 16 029 controls, found that the risk of suicidal ideation or behaviour was about twice as great in the drug treatment groups (0.43%) as in those given placebo (0.22%). The relative risk was greater in patients with epilepsy than in those with other disorders. Drugs implicated by this analy- sis were carbamazepine, felbamate, gabapentin, lamotrig- ine, levetiracetam, oxcarbazepine, pregabalin, tiagabine, topiramate, valproate, and zonisamide. However, the FDA considered that the increased risk was a class effect that would be shared by all antiepileptics. It was recommended that prescribers and patients and their families should be aware of the risk, and should be alert for behavioural changes and other warning signs that might signal suicidal ideation.
